input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view in the Dashboard

## Description

Deliver a run comparison surface in the Dashboard: users can select two or
more training and pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by
side, and, for two selected runs, switch to a diff presentation that highlights
which parameters and metrics changed. This replaces the current workflow of
exporting run data to spreadsheets for comparison.

## Scope

- Run selection from the runs list: a user can select two or more runs and
  open the comparison.
- Side-by-side presentation of each selected run's parameters and metrics in a
  single comparison view.
- Diff presentation for two selected runs: values that differ between the two
  runs are highlighted so changed parameters and metrics are immediately
  visible; unchanged values remain distinguishable.
- The comparison reads run parameters and metrics through the Dashboard's
  existing run data sources (including the KFP v2 interface for pipeline
  runs); no changes to the run-producing backends are in scope.
- The comparison works for both training runs and pipeline runs within a
  project. Comparison across clusters or across projects is out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a list of runs, when a user selects two or more runs and opens the
  comparison, then the parameters and metrics of every selected run are
  displayed side by side in a single view.
- Given two runs displayed in the comparison, when the user switches to the
  diff presentation, then the parameters and metrics that differ between the
  two runs are highlighted and unchanged values are distinguishable.
- Given pipeline runs and training runs in the same project, when either kind
  is included in a selection, then their parameters and metrics are retrieved
  through the existing run data interfaces and rendered in the comparison.
- Given a selection that includes a run with missing parameters or metrics,
  then the comparison renders the available values without failing the whole
  view.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard — fully covered by this epic.
- **HLR-3 (P1, bundled)**: the run "diff" view highlighting which parameters
  and metrics changed between two selected runs is a presentation mode of the
  same comparison surface over the same run data, in the same component and
  team — bundled into this epic at the higher priority (P0) rather than split
  into a separate epic, because splitting would build the same surface twice
  and add an artificial serialization boundary.

# Confirm Data Science Pipelines run data supports run comparison

## Description

The Data Science Pipelines team confirms that pipeline run parameters and
metrics are available through the component's existing interfaces in the form
the Dashboard run comparison requires, and that Data Science Pipelines keeps
working without code changes for this capability. This is the validation of a
passive component: the comparison consumes pipeline run data but does not
change the pipelines component itself.

## Scope

- Confirm that per-run parameters and metrics for pipeline runs are retrievable
  through the existing KFP v2 interface for arbitrary sets of runs, in the form
  the comparison view consumes (per-run key/value parameters and metrics).
- Confirm representative pipeline runs of the kind data scientists compare
  (training and evaluation runs) exercise the retrieval as the comparison will
  use it.
- Confirm no Data Science Pipelines code changes are required; document any
  gaps found together with recommended follow-up work.
- Produce a short validation report recording the checks performed and their
  outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists that documents retrieval of parameters and
  metrics for representative pipeline runs through the existing KFP v2
  interface, in the form the run comparison consumes.
- The report confirms that Data Science Pipelines requires no code changes for
  the run comparison capability, or enumerates concrete gaps with recommended
  follow-up work.
- The validation exercises multiple runs within a single project, matching the
  comparison's selection model.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0, supporting)**: this epic does not solely cover an HLR; it
  validates the Data Science Pipelines component that supplies pipeline-run
  parameters and metrics for the side-by-side and diff comparison. The passive
  component is owned by a different team than the Dashboard comparison work,
  so its validation is tracked as this separate epic rather than as an
  acceptance criterion on the Dashboard epic.

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions record the run that produced them, and that linkage
is exposed through the Model Registry so clients can resolve the producing run
for a given model version. This is the data foundation that lets a comparison
be opened starting from the Model Registry.

## Scope

- Capture the producing-run reference on a registered model version at
  registration time, when the producing run is known.
- Expose the producing-run linkage as model version metadata through the Model
  Registry's existing metadata extension point (custom properties on model
  versions, per the architecture context), so clients can retrieve it for a
  given model version.
- Keep registration backward compatible: model versions registered without run
  information remain valid and fully functional.
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion, and any comparison
  logic (the comparison surface itself lives in the Dashboard).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a known run, then the producing run's
  reference is recorded on the model version and retrievable through the Model
  Registry interface by a client that knows only the model version.
- Given a model version registered without run information, then registration
  succeeds and the model version remains valid and queryable.
- Given an existing model version registered before this change, then it
  remains valid and readable with no migration required.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1, data half)**: "registered model versions link back to the run
  that produced them" — the linkage data and its exposure are delivered by
  this epic. The registry-side entry point that opens a comparison from this
  linkage is the Dashboard's registry integration and is covered separately.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

From the Model Registry view in the Dashboard, a user can follow a registered
model version to the run that produced it and open the run comparison for that
run. This gives model promotion decisions a path from registered artifacts
back to the experiment evidence.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry UI, surface the producing-run linkage
  recorded on registered model versions.
- Provide an entry point on a model version that opens the run comparison
  including its producing run, so the user lands in the comparison workflow
  without navigating through the runs list.
- Degrade gracefully when a model version has no recorded producing run: the
  entry point is absent or clearly disabled, with no error shown to the user.
- Out of scope: comparison across projects or clusters, and any change to how
  lineage is stored in the Model Registry itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a recorded producing run, when the
  user opens that model version in the Model Registry view, then an entry
  point is available that opens the run comparison including that run.
- Given a model version without a recorded producing run, when the user opens
  it in the Model Registry view, then the entry point is absent or clearly
  disabled and no error is raised.
- Given the comparison opened from a model version, then the user can add
  further runs to the comparison from within the comparison workflow.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1, UI half)**: "so a comparison can be opened from the Model
  Registry" — the registry-side entry point and navigation into the comparison
  are delivered by this epic, building on the run comparison surface and on
  the producing-run linkage recorded on model versions.

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

User documentation for the run comparison capability, covering the workflow
from both entry points: selecting runs from the runs list, and following a
registered model version from the Model Registry to its producing run.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparison from the runs list: how to select two or more runs, open the
  side-by-side parameters and metrics view, and read the two-run diff
  presentation that highlights changed values.
- Comparison from the Model Registry: how a registered model version links to
  its producing run and how to open the comparison from there, including
  adding further runs to the comparison.
- Guidance on what the comparison covers (training and pipeline runs within a
  project) and what is out of scope (cross-project and cross-cluster
  comparison).
- Screenshots and captions for the comparison views and the registry entry
  point, reflecting the implemented behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the
  runs list, including multi-run side-by-side comparison and the two-run diff
  view.
- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the
  Model Registry, following a model version to its producing run.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  comparison behavior before publication, and screenshots match the shipped
  UI.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry — fully covered by this epic. Priority follows
  the docs-authoring exception (strategy priority Major → P1).
